data.long_meaning: The name Bala originates from the Sanskrit language and means 'Child' or 'Young One'. In Hindu mythology, Bala is a name given to various gods and goddesses, including Lord Ganesha and Goddess Parvati. It is a name of reverence and respect, symbolizing innocence, purity, and the beginning of a new life. The name Bala carries the meaning “Child, Young One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bala usually hope their child will grow to embody child, young one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bala holds great cultural significance in Hinduism. It is a term of deep love and affection used to address a young child. In Indian culture, children are considered the epitome of joy, hope, and innocence. Naming a child Bala expresses the deep attachment and desire for the child to maintain his/her inner child, preserving the pure joy and wonderment of childhood.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Bala can be found in the Hindu belief of preserving and reverencing the divine child within oneself. It is a reminder to remain childlike in one's spiritual journey, letting go of ego and attachment, and embracing the childlike qualities of awe, curiosity, and wonder. Goddess Parvati, who is known as the embodiment of love and compassion, is also referred to as Bala. In the Bhagavad Gita, Lord Krishna encourages Arjuna to "see in all beings the same Self, the same Eternal, the same Bala." This phrase conveys the idea that all beings are children of the divine, and we should approach all interactions with love, compassion, and respect.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bala, meaning 'child' or 'infant' in Sanskrit, symbolizes the innocence, purity, and playful spirit of youth. It is a name evoking the boundless energy, curiosity, and joy of childhood, reminding us to approach life with the same spirit of wonder and delight.

vedic_reference.note: Bala is a popular name in Hindu mythology and is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures. It is the name of Lord Vishnu in his infant form and is also used as a name for boys born in the auspicious Hindu month of Baishakha (April-May).

historical_references.reference: Bala is a name mentioned in the Mahabharata, where it is used to refer to Balarama, the elder brother of Krishna.

trends: Bala is a common name for boys in India and Nepal.
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Bala remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
